target_customer: Ice cream shops, foodservice operators and retail shoppers who want dairy-like plant-based products
problem: Plant-based dairy has not matched the taste, texture and functionality of conventional dairy, so many consumers will not switch.
business_model: CPG and foodservice sales of plant-based ice cream and soft serve mixes, expanding to a plant-based dairy ingredient platform

founders.name: Aylon Steinhart
education: UC Berkeley Haas School of Business, graduated cum laude
founders.background_notes: YC page says he incubated dozens of startups at the Good Food Institute and has worked with Nestle and Kellogg's, nature of that work not stated.

founders.name: Thomas Elliott Bowman
prior_employers: Restaurants holding a combined 16 Michelin stars
founders.background_notes: Series B press release calls him a food scientist and chef nominated for a James Beard Award. The company site calls its chef and co-founder one with restaurants totaling 16 Michelin stars.

competitors.name: Perfect Day
competitors.what: Animal-free dairy proteins made by microbial fermentation, with a limited ice cream run
competitors.traction_then: Limited ice cream release described in a profile
competitors.funding_then: Not verified from an opened source

technical_complexity.rationale: Reproducing dairy functionality from plant ingredients using micelles needed food science R&D, formulation and scale-up to manufacturing.

defensibility.rationale: Formulation know how and trade secrets help, but large dairy and plant-milk brands could copy products once the category is proven.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbent frozen dessert brands sold dairy-free lines but no incumbent acquired Eclipse as of the sources found.

market_need_then: Plant-based meat had shown strong consumer demand, and dairy alternatives were growing but lagged on taste and texture, which is the gap the company stated in its pitch.

branding.domain_note: Uses eclipsefoods.com, not a bare eclipse.com (source: company site).

identity.visual_style: colorful homepage, and 2025 packaging inspired by Hokkaido, Japan dairy region
identity.voice_and_tone: mission driven, claims molecule for molecule dairy match

branding.brand_signature: Plant-based dairy built from micelles, the microscopic magic of milk
branding.community_and_virality: Coverage from CNN, SF Chronicle, Forbes and TechCrunch, and a Whole Foods deal in November 2021.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong press and star investors and retail deals at Whole Foods, but a regional consumer brand without evidence of a cult following.

pivots.to: Full service plant-based dairy provider across several categories
pivots.why: Series B coverage says funds would move the company beyond ice cream.

outcome_analysis: Eclipse raised a $12M Series A in November 2020 led by Forerunner and a Series B of over $40M in June 2022 led by Sozo, reaching over $60M raised, and grew retail through Whole Foods. It is still active with no exit. A 2023 Class II recall of one product was seen in a single database. The outcome is open but funding momentum was strong.
notes: Seed round before the Series A not found. Perfect Day competitor source was returned by search but the page was blocked (403), so its details are from the search summary and are thin. Rivals named in the 2020 Series A article (SO Delicious, Coconut Bliss, Oatly) are not used as they are dated more than a year after the batch. Recall of caramel butter pecan cup 2023-06-30 appears in a single database (regdatalab), unverified. Series B stated by PR Newswire and several outlets, 'over $40M'.
